summary: A thin, flexible, carnivorous plant that traps and eats bugs: it ensnares tiny insects with its vines and devours them, blindingly fast when catching prey, and flings a vine at anything it notices moving. It soaks up water through its root feet planted deep in the ground, but can't escape while rooted; instead its thin body bends and sways to avoid any attack, and it spits a corrosive fluid that melts even iron. It prefers hot, humid places. Its bud looks like a human face, which is why it is rumoured to be a legendary mandrake. In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives on Routes 31, 32 and 44 in Johto and Routes 24, 25, 5 and 6 in Kanto.

anatomy.text: A thin plant with a bud for a head (Gen 4 shape humanoid), 0.7 m and 4.0 kg, typed Grass and Poison: the Flower Pokémon.
A thin, flexible, extremely skinny body; root feet; vines.
From its mouth it spits, or leaks, a corrosive fluid that melts even iron.
Its bud looks like a human face.

diet.text: A carnivorous Pokémon that traps and eats bugs: it ensnares tiny insects with its vines and devours them.
diet.analogy: Real carnivorous plants, such as sundews and Venus flytraps, catch insects for the nitrogen poor soil lacks.

diet.text: It is blindingly fast, and quick, at capturing prey with its vines.
It soaks up the moisture it needs through its root feet, planted deep underground.

habitat.text: Hot and humid places; the Gen 3 Pokédex habitat is forest.
In HeartGold and SoulSilver it lives on Routes 31, 32 and 44 in Johto and Routes 24, 25, 5 and 6 in Kanto (most on Route 24, 60%), at any time, in both versions; the Johto Safari Zone has it too.

behavior.text: If it notices anything that moves, it immediately flings its vine at the object.
It plants its feet deep underground to replenish water.
Its activity pattern is not stated; the tables have it at any time.

social.text: Nothing is said about Bellsprout living together. Its final form is said to live in huge colonies deep in jungles (71.1).

reproduction.text: Grass egg group, 20 egg cycles, an even sex ratio, medium-slow growth. Nothing describes how it breeds.

defense.text: Its thin and flexible body lets it bend and sway to avoid any attack, however strong.
While rooted, it can't escape its enemy.
Sleep Powder (Lv 13), Poison Powder (Lv 15), Stun Spore (Lv 17) and Acid (Lv 23): powders and the iron-melting fluid.

life_cycle.text: It becomes Weepinbell at level 21 and Victreebel with a Leaf Stone: 0.7 m and 4.0 kg, then 1.0 m and 6.4 kg, then 1.7 m and 15.5 kg.
Read as development, a bug-catcher grows into a swallower of anything that moves (70.2) and then a lure-and-swallow trap (71.2).

moves_in_the_wild.text: Vine Whip, Growth, Wrap, Sleep Powder, Poison Powder, Stun Spore, Acid, Knock Off, Sweet Scent, Gastro Acid, Razor Leaf, Slam and Wring Out: vines, powders and acid.

ecology.text: A plant that eats insects: a producer and a predator at once.
On Kanto's Routes 24, 25, 5 and 6 it shares the grass with Oddish, Abra and Pidgey; on Route 44 with Weepinbell, Tangela, Lickitung and Poliwhirl.

humans.text: Because its bud looks like a human face, it is rumoured to be a type of legendary mandrake plant.

homestead.text: A living bug-trap for the garden: it eats insects.
Its fluid melts even iron: keep it away from tools and the plough.
It flings a vine at anything that moves: warn children.
The greenhouse in July, hot and wet, and three Bellsprout snapping at the whitefly.

microhabitat: hot, humid grass and forest edges
niche.foraging: ensnares tiny insects with its vines and devours them

ecotypes.name: Rooted bug-trap
ecotypes.reading: A lineage that stays put: it roots deep, drains insects and heals in the sun. Fits hot, humid, sunny ground with many insects.
ecotypes.behavior: Rarely uproots; lets the insects come.

ecotypes.name: Swaying dodger
ecotypes.reading: The thin body that bends and sways out of any attack (69.6), as a way of fighting: a dance, a distraction, a leaf that never misses. Fits open windy grass.
ecotypes.behavior: Sways in the wind and strikes from the sway.

open_questions: Which insects does Bellsprout eat, and how many?
Does it move about, or stay rooted most of its life?
Why does a plant that prefers hot, humid places live on cool Kanto routes?
Where are Victreebel's 'huge colonies deep in jungles'?

folklore.text: Because its bud looks like a human face, it is rumoured to be a type of legendary mandrake plant.
